note: This module has NO configuration, no schema, no permissions, no Drush and no plugins. Its entire effect is a single hook_entity_type_alter() that unsets core's 'EntityUntranslatableFields' validation constraint from every entity type (via the service remove_entity_untranslatable_field_validation.entity_modifier). Easy cases quiz the mechanism. Medium cases are grounded in live state: one asks the agent to identify the module responsible for node lacking the constraint; the other installs a known untranslatable field and reads it back. NO hard/execution tier is provided, deliberately: the module's only effect is a global, always-on constraint removal that is not a per-build artifact, and it is only observable during an in-memory edit/validate cycle - untranslatable field values are SHARED across translations, so after a save+reload the value is identical in every language and core's transient constraint no longer fires, making a reload-based live-state verify unable to distinguish the module's presence. The only way to force a failing reset state is to disable the module, which triggers a full container rebuild - unsafe and disruptive on this shared site. Authoring a contrived hard case that does not actually test the module would be dishonest, so it is omitted with this justification.

evals.prompt: What does the Drupal module remove_entity_untranslatable_field_validation do, and which core validation constraint does it remove?
evals.expected_output: It removes core's EntityUntranslatableFields validation constraint from every entity type, so untranslatable ('shared') fields can be changed while editing a non-default translation without a validation error.

evals.prompt: How does remove_entity_untranslatable_field_validation actually remove the constraint? Name the hook and the service/method it uses.
evals.expected_output: A single hook_entity_type_alter() implementation calls the remove_entity_untranslatable_field_validation.entity_modifier service (EntityModifier::removeUntranslatableEntityFieldValidation()), which loops all entity types and unsets the 'EntityUntranslatableFields' constraint.

evals.prompt: Does remove_entity_untranslatable_field_validation let me choose which entity types are affected, and how would I confirm on a running site that it is active?
evals.expected_output: No - it is global and unconditional: it strips the constraint from ALL entity types (there is no settings form). Confirm by checking a translatable entity type: \Drupal::entityTypeManager()->getDefinition('node')->getConstraints() no longer contains an 'EntityUntranslatableFields' key.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the node entity type does NOT have the core 'EntityUntranslatableFields' validation constraint. Inspect the site and identify which enabled contrib module is responsible for removing it.
evals.expected_output: The remove_entity_untranslatable_field_validation module removes it (via hook_entity_type_alter); inspecting node's constraints shows EntityUntranslatableFields is absent.

evals.prompt: This site has a translation-enabled content type 'ruftv_med' with one added field that is configured as NOT translatable. Inspect the live field configuration and give the machine name of that untranslatable field.
evals.expected_output: field_ruftv_med - its FieldConfig on node.ruftv_med has translatable = false; because remove_entity_untranslatable_field_validation is enabled, editors can still change it from a non-default translation without a validation error.
